verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              स श्वेतपर्वतं वीरः समतिक्रम्य वीर्यवान्। देशं किंपुरुषावासं द्रुमपुत्रेण रक्षितम्॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said After having crossed the white mountains, that greatly powerful hero conquered the country of the Kimpurushas which was ruled by Drumaputra.

verses.sanskrit: महता सन्निपातेन क्षत्रियान्तकरेण ह। अजयत्पाण्डवश्रेष्ठः करे चैनं न्यवेशयत्॥२॥
verses.english: After a great battle in which great was the slaughter of Kshatriyas, that best of the Pandavas brought the country under his complete control.

verses.sanskrit: तं जित्वा हाटकं नाम देशं गुह्यकरक्षितम्। पाकशासनिरव्यग्रः सह सैन्यः समासदत्॥३॥
verses.english: Having conquered this country the son of Indra with a determined mind and with a large number of troops, subjugated the country, named Hataka, ruled by the Guhyakas.

verses.sanskrit: तांस्तु सान्त्वेन निर्जित्य मानसं सर उत्तमम्। ऋषिकुल्यास्तथा सर्वा ददर्श कुरुनन्दनः॥४॥
verses.english: Having subjugated them by a policy of conciliation, that descendant of Kuru saw that excellent lake, called Manasa. He saw also various other lakes and tanks sacred to the Rishis.

verses.sanskrit: सरो मानसमासाद्य हाटकानभितः प्रभुः। गन्धर्वरक्षितं देशमजयत्पाण्डवस्ततः॥५॥
verses.english: Having arrived at the Manasa (lake), the lord Pandava (Arjuna) conquered the regions, ruled by the Gandharvas the regions that lay around the Hataka countries.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र तित्तिरिकल्माषान्मण्डूकाख्यान्हयोत्तमान्। लेभे स करमत्यन्तं गन्धर्वनगरात्तदा॥६॥
verses.english: The victor (Arjuna) took from the city of the Gandharvas as his tribute many excellent horses, called Tittiri, Kalmasha and Manduka.

verses.sanskrit: उत्तरं हरिवर्षं तु स समासाद्य पाण्डवः। इयेष जेतुं तं देशं पाकशासनन्दनः॥७॥
verses.english: Wishing to conquer that country, the son of Indra, the Pandava (Arjuna), came to the country of North Harivarsha.

verses.sanskrit: तत एनं महावीर्यं महाकाया महाबलाः। द्वारपालाः समासाद्य हृष्टा वचनमब्रुवन्॥८॥
verses.english: Thereupon some greatly powerful strong and huge-bodied frontier guards came to him and his cheerfully spoke to him.

verses.sanskrit: पार्थ नेदं त्वया शक्यं पुरं जेतुं कथञ्चन। उपावर्तस्व कल्याण पर्याप्तमिदमच्युत॥९॥
verses.english: "O Partha, this country cannot be conquered by you. If you seek your good return from this place. O Achyuta, your conquests are already enough.

verses.sanskrit: इदं पुरं यः प्रविशेद्घ्रुवं न स भवेन्नरः। प्रीयामहे त्वया वीर पर्याप्तो विजयस्तव॥१०॥
verses.english: He that enters this country, if he is human, is sure to perish. We are pleased with you, your conquests are (already) too many.

verses.sanskrit: न चात्र किञ्चिज्जेतव्यमर्जुनात्र प्रदृश्यते। उत्तराः कुरुवो ह्येते नात्र युद्धं प्रवर्तते॥११॥
verses.english: O Arjuna, there is nothing to be seen here, there is nothing to be conquered here by you. The Northern Kurus live here, there cannot be any war here.

verses.sanskrit: प्रविष्टोऽपि हि कौन्तेय नेह द्रक्ष्यसि किञ्चन। न हि मानुषदेहेन शक्यमत्राभिवीक्षितुम्॥१२॥
verses.english: O son of Kunti, even if you enter this country, you will not be able to seen any thing, for nothing can be seen here with human eyes.

verses.sanskrit: अथेह पुरुषव्याघ्र किञ्चिदन्यच्चिकीर्षसि। तत्प्रब्रूहि करिष्यामो वचनात्तव भारत॥१३॥
verses.english: O best of men, O descendant of Bharata, if however, you desire to have any thing else, tell us, we may do your bidding."

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तानब्रवीद्राजन्नर्जुनः प्रहसन्निव। पार्थिवत्वं चिकीर्षामि धर्मराजश्च धीमतः॥१४॥
verses.english: Having been thus addressed, Arjuna smilingly thus spoke to them, “I desire the acquisition of the imperial dignity for the intelligent Dharamaraja Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: न प्रवेक्ष्यामि वो देशं विरुद्धं यदि मानुषैः। युधिष्ठिराय यत्किञ्चित्करपण्यं प्रदीयताम्॥१५॥
verses.english: If this country is shut against human beings, I shall not enter it. Let something be given by you as tribute to Yudhishthira.

verses.sanskrit: ततो दिव्यानि वस्त्राणि दिव्यान्याभरणानि च। क्षौमाजिनानि दिव्यानि तस्य ते प्रददुः करम्॥१६॥
verses.english: Thereupon they gave him as tribute many celestials clothes and ornaments and many celestials silks and celestials skins.

verses.sanskrit: एवं स पुरुषव्याघ्रो विजित्य दिशमुत्तराम्। सङ्ग्रामान्सुबहून्कृत्वा क्षत्रियैर्दस्युभिस्तथा॥१७॥
verses.english: It was thus that best of men (Arjuna) conquered the northern countries, and all the kings (of those countries); and he fought many battles both with the Kshatriyas and the robber tribes.
verses.bhavadeepa: क्षुमाऽतसीविशेषः ’क्षुमाऽतसी नीलिकयोः' इति मेदिनी । तत्तन्तुनिर्मितानि क्षौमाणि अजिनानि च ॥१६॥

verses.sanskrit: स विनिर्जित्य राज्ञस्तान्करे च विनिवेश्य तु। धनान्यादाय सर्वेभ्यो रत्नानि विविधानि च॥१८॥
verses.english: Having thus vanquished and subjugated many kings and countries, he exacted tributes from them all, and (he thus) obtained much wealth and many gems and jewels.

verses.sanskrit: हयांस्तित्तिरिकल्माषाञ्च्छुकपत्रनिभानपि। मयूरसदृशान्यान्सर्वाननिलरंहसः॥१९॥
verses.english: And many swift horses of the species called Tittiri and Kalmasha, and also many others with the colour of peacocks.

verses.sanskrit: वृतः सुमहता राजन्बलेन चतुरङ्गिणा। आजगाम पुनर्वीरः शक्रप्रस्थं पुरोत्तमम्॥२०॥
verses.english: O king, surrounded by a large army of the four kinds of troops, the hero (at last) returned to the city of Indraprastha.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मराजाय तत्पार्थो धनं सर्वं सवाहनम्। न्यवेदयदनुज्ञातस्तेन राज्ञा गृहान्ययौ॥२१॥
verses.english: Partha (Arjuna) offered to Dharmaraja all the wealth and the animals brought by him. Commanded by the king, the hero went to his chamber to take rest.
